sections.title: First Law of Thermodynamics
sections.content: Energy can neither be created nor destroyed. The change in internal energy of a system equals the heat added to the system minus the work done by the system.

sections.title: Enthalpy
sections.content: Enthalpy is a state function defined for constant-pressure processes. The enthalpy change of a reaction equals the heat absorbed or released at constant pressure.

sections.title: Second Law and Entropy
sections.content: The entropy of an isolated system always increases in a spontaneous process. Entropy is a measure of disorder or the number of accessible microstates.

sections.title: Gibbs Free Energy
sections.content: Gibbs free energy combines enthalpy and entropy to predict spontaneity at constant T and P. A negative ΔG indicates a spontaneous process.
